clauses.operation: Capture, continuation-copy, shared-tail discovery and cross-context export
clauses.premise: A logical frame/segment domain survives address movement; overlapping captures share domains; wrapper identity does not identify the aliased payload
clauses.realization: Rooted domain records and nonreused incarnation, wrapper selection stamp, domain content/topology revisions and separate relocation epoch; register before aliases escape
clauses.failure: Unproved overlap, exhausted incarnation or unknown stack owner refuses optimized export and retains source custody
clauses.sourceGap: Current copy shares raw frame and denv fields but creates no canonical domain or managed alias publication

clauses.operation: Copy wrapper and prepare the next restore fragment
clauses.premise: Authentic view issuance reads authoritative rooted head/denv and the admitted fragment under an access lease; allocation cannot lose the source
clauses.realization: Preallocate rooted metadata at a complete checkpoint, capture a consistent wrapper selection, preserve shared payload identities and give the new wrapper its own selection record
clauses.failure: Allocation or registration failure leaves original roots owned; no ACK or complete-view publication on unknown outcome
clauses.sourceGap: continuation-copy allocates a shallow wrapper and check-heap may collect; source adapters and issuance evidence are absent

clauses.operation: frame-set!, continuation-set!, initialization stores and admitted frame reflection
clauses.premise: All readers/writers of a shared physical field obey C synchronization; a logical store invalidates every dependent view through its shared domain
clauses.realization: Reserve noncollecting remembered-log capacity before the short write lease; validate slot role via FrameSpec; perform store and revision publication under exclusion; release publishes to acquiring readers
clauses.failure: Log overflow or capacity failure releases lease before a safe collecting retry; root value retained; partial/unknown writes keep domain unresolved
clauses.sourceGap: Current setters perform plain C stores under local not-interrupts-enabled declarations, not interprocessor ownership enforcement

clauses.operation: continuation-frame-set!, denv-set!, next!, structural-link changes and scheduler save/restore
clauses.premise: Wrapper head/denv selection is a coherent pair; membership and ordering of dependent domains cannot change unnoticed
clauses.realization: Wrapper selection revision covers its head/denv; link-domain topology revisions cover shared tails; compare exact ordered domain/incarnation/revision lists, never an unchecked hash or sum
clauses.failure: Changed topology invalidates certificate and triggers rooted rediscovery; scheduler-owned slot consumption never consumes a general full continuation
clauses.sourceGap: next! mutates wrapper fields and sometimes stack RA; raw link/RA setters cannot be treated as ordinary payload stores

clauses.operation: GC heapification, forwarding, root repair and post-GC reload
clauses.premise: Logical slot values use Scheme object identity; relocation changes physical coordinates without changing logical payload revisions
clauses.realization: Frozen context/domain access authorizes one structural updater; collector updates every authoritative root/handle; a fresh relocation epoch revokes raw address caches before resume
clauses.failure: Unsettled native borrow or missing frozen root view denies movement; matching logical revision never authorizes reuse of an old address
clauses.sourceGap: Collector frame access is VM-wide and distinct from raw mutator stores; stable identity and complete address reload correspondence remain unimplemented

clauses.operation: Validate a prepared fragment after writes, GC or winding
clauses.premise: Issuance is authentic and complete relevant writer histories are represented; equality includes domain membership, incarnation and revisions
clauses.realization: For one fixed certificate scope, use a ghost serial history to interpret Lean ImageHistory; physical dependency vectors are evidence for unchanged history, not a global VM counter
clauses.failure: Counter wrap/reuse, incomplete writers or changed scope expires certificate; reissue under new scope; finite Quint ticket IDs do not prove unbounded implementation traces
clauses.sourceGap: The existing Lean scalar version is an abstraction premise; no source refinement of a distributed revision vector exists yet

clauses.operation: Graft/return installation and each break-handler caller restoration
clauses.premise: Coherence is required at the actual fragment-consumption point; an invocation-wide frozen snapshot must not hide later legal writes to its unconsumed tail
clauses.realization: Retain rooted tail selection, pre-reserve bounded destination space, acquire short source read leases and current context grant, copy one admitted fragment into private execution storage, then release; revalidate next fragment when reached
clauses.failure: Insufficient contiguous reserve or stale certificate returns to complete rooted checkpoint before copy; partial initialization cannot be published as an executable frame
clauses.sourceGap: Current break handler restores a reached caller frame and rewrites links; no complete generated modern-C fragment adapter or whole-round capacity proof

clauses.operation: Scheme wind hooks and multiple restoration of saved hook suffixes
clauses.premise: User hooks run without physical frame leases; restored Scheme suffixes acquire new physical permission; unchanged winding policy owns observable effects
clauses.realization: Keep logical transfer roots and selected Scheme continuation, release C leases before hook, then reread/reload current source fields and reissue only physical certificates; do not replay completed hooks merely because addresses changed
clauses.failure: Abandoned helper completion is stale while legal Scheme suffix remains reusable; native origin expiration refuses only the unsupported C return
clauses.sourceGap: Source winding computes a destination then invokes hooks; graft later reads actual continuation fields, so automatic semantic replanning is not justified

clauses.operation: Denv/winder vector mutation, referenced Scheme objects and deserialized shells
clauses.premise: Denv identity is not deep immutability; referenced heap effects remain shared; derived cached fields need their own synchronization and dependency coverage
clauses.realization: Distinguish wrapper selection, shared record field changes, ordinary shared referents and private execution stores; initialization records remain scannable and non-executable until complete
clauses.failure: Unsupported alias/native writer removes optimized admission; conservative scanning alone cannot repair a C data race
clauses.sourceGap: Denv records are vectors, serializers fill shells and I/O rebuild writes separate frame objects; complete indirect writer coverage remains open

clauses.operation: Publish a stack-backed capture for another execution context or collector
clauses.premise: Local lazy capture may remain stack-backed; cross-context access requires a frozen owner view or a fully initialized managed shared representation before publication
clauses.realization: Use existing root-transfer custody boundary: register destination before source ACK, preserve native-origin identity, publish shared status before withdrawing private-owner privileges
clauses.failure: Unknown owner writes cannot be guessed stopped; no unrestricted foreign writer is isolated without a proven physical access bound
clauses.sourceGap: Same-VM cross-context export, writer withdrawal and destination registration do not yet form a complete implemented adapter

criteria.necessary: Multiple mutators execute in the same VM without a VM-wide lock across Scheme work or hooks
criteria.observation: Actual simultaneous active contexts with correct shared heap/control observations; processor population alone is insufficient
criteria.limitation: Frame aliases cover only part of the shared heap memory model; existing Quint is a bounded single aggregate control model

criteria.necessary: Read sharing and disjoint frame domains proceed independently; only overlapping writes/copiers serialize locally
criteria.observation: Concurrent distinct-domain restoration and collection with contention/work counts; no global frame gate on the hot path
criteria.limitation: A per-domain lock design alone proves neither fairness nor speedup

criteria.necessary: Context owns roots, participant owns epoch authorization and worker owns claimed copying tasks independently of carrier ID
criteria.observation: Worker count and root-origin count need not match; each claimed task updates the correct frozen roots and phase
criteria.limitation: Current source still indexes participants/completion by carrier and checks synchronous binding

criteria.necessary: Unknown outcomes retain exact roots/resources; isolation requires known writable intervals and physical stop or exclusion
criteria.observation: Distinguish healthy other-VM GC from progress inside the affected VM; test known quarantine bounds and unresolved writes
criteria.limitation: Current moving arena may remain blocked by unknown writes; alias records do not magically enable selective collection

criteria.necessary: Frozen roots, publishing/private/Tail work, weak cleanup, termination and contiguous reserve form one admitted round
criteria.observation: No unfinished task is hidden by carrier-idle counts; capacity failure retains source before flip under unchanged limits
criteria.limitation: These GC/capacity obligations are dependencies, not proved by CS-BRIDGE/CS-WRITERS or the existing Lean law

criteria.necessary: Parallel useful work exceeds access, root, barrier, dispatch and retention overhead for a stated workload
criteria.observation: Same-source/profile single-versus-multicore work, latency, throughput and physical peak; include ordinary fast paths and failure histories
criteria.limitation: No measured scaling result in this research; Scheme map ordering is preserved

benefits.avoided: No repeated eager whole-chain snapshot by the new adapter; preserve existing reached-frame restoration
benefits.added: Per-fragment grant, root reload and dependency validation; copy reached payload and perform required hooks
benefits.condition: For r shots compare actual reached words sum(Rj), not r times an invented full-image baseline

benefits.avoided: No scan of all A wrapper aliases and no global historical identity table for each payload write
benefits.added: O(1) revision work per touched admitted domain and O(d) validation per certificate with d dependencies
benefits.condition: Canonical shared-tail domains and complete writers; multi-domain operations pay for every touched domain

benefits.avoided: Address-only changes need not rebuild logically unchanged payload or rerun winding effects
benefits.added: All authoritative root updates and physical address reload remain mandatory
benefits.condition: Stable logical identity, frozen access and complete reload; pointer equality or matching logical revision alone is insufficient

benefits.avoided: Unnecessary VM-wide serialization of independent frame copies/readers
benefits.added: Domain metadata, local contention, task accounting and coordinator publication
benefits.condition: For P workers and serial fraction s, ideal speedup is bounded by 1/(s+(1-s)/P) before extra overhead; neither s nor realized speedup measured

benefits.avoided: Share eligible capture payload across wrappers and invocations rather than cloning all tails up front
benefits.added: O(A+D+sum(dj)) wrapper/domain/live-certificate metadata plus rooted transfer, active copies and GC/native reserves
benefits.condition: D is live canonical domains, not unbounded request history; retained unknown observers prevent unsafe domain reuse

benefits.avoided: Eligible clean mature frame payload can eventually skip repeated minor traversal
benefits.added: Remembered stores, overflow handling, scans and promotion/resume reserve
benefits.condition: Zero claimed gain until all writers and generational runtime qualify; ordinary root visits and relocation are not eliminated

witnesses.finding: Wrapper allocation shares frame/denv and checks heap afterwards
Plain heap/stack stores use descriptor-derived coordinates
Frame materialization can collect; wrapper frame/denv setters are separate
next! updates wrapper selection and stack RA; copied wrappers may share tails
Break handler copies one reached caller frame from stack or heap
Graft reads actual continuation frame/denv and installs current thread caches
Capture can publish a stack-backed frame selection through a break frame
GC copies frame payload and repairs forwarding/structural roots
Ordinary slots, link and return address have distinct scan roles
Denv, environment and dynwind data use mutable vector records
Deserializer registers shells and fills continuation/frame values recursively
Separate explode/implode path creates and fills frame objects
Collector frame gate is VM-wide; raw reflective setters do not call it
Worker scans the supplied frozen participant context, registers, startup marker and RC roots
Dispatch and strong completion still use carrier processor ID
GC requires synchronous carrier/context binding and checks unknown-resize isolation
Scheme computes destination winding and calls a suffix that invokes current continuation fields
